feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 4 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.35) is the best design so far, with oval progress 0.710, score 188.0, and line losses of 1.2 (oval), 1.0 (s-bend) and 1.4 (slalom). Those counts show the 50 mm span is not losing the tape, so the geometry should stay as it is. Iteration 0 (40 mm) and iteration 3 (60 mm) show that span drives progress, and iteration 1 shows that y 0.03 collapses progress, so keep y 0.05. max_error has stayed at 0.059 to 0.065 m in every iteration, and span, footprint and lead have not moved it. The next race will test whether controller speed and damping change that. Decide from it as follows. If max_error falls below about 0.058 m and oval progress holds at 0.65 or more, keep the 50 mm span and change nothing in the geometry. If max_error stays on its plateau (0.059 to 0.065 m) while oval progress holds, the excursions are not speed-limited, so the next geometry test is wheel_track 0.10. If progress falls below about 0.5 because the robot is too slow to finish, restore base_speed to 1.5 and keep the span.
requested_changes: If max_error stays at 0.059 to 0.065 m with oval progress at 0.65 or more, change wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 with no other geometry change. Iteration 4 showed max_error on its plateau at every span, footprint and lead, so turn rate is the untested lever.

If oval progress drops below about 0.5 while line losses stay near 1, keep the 50 mm span, footprint 0.012 and y 0.05, and tell the Integrator that the speed change is the cause. Do not move the span, since iteration 0 (40 mm) and iteration 4 (50 mm) both reached progress above 0.66 and the span is not the cause.

Keep y at 0.05 and the 12 mm footprint. Iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 cut oval progress to 0.273, and iteration 3 showed that 12 mm at 60 mm span gave 0.275, so the 50 mm span with 12 mm footprint is the proven base.
